triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '1. Treating sm_120 as if it were sm_100 (the biggest framing trap)' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 1. Treating sm_120 as if it were sm_100 (the biggest framing trap)

problem.statement: CuTeDSL GDN Decode on sm_120 — Pitfalls -- 1. Treating sm_120 as if it were sm_100 (the biggest framing trap)

payload.attempted: "Blackwell is Blackwell, just port the SM100 wgmma/tcgen05 GEMM."
payload.lesson: **Hopper TMA + Ampere warp ALU**. This is also documented in the sister project `` — same chip, same constraint.

established_fact.mechanism: sm_120 is **client Blackwell** (RTX PRO 5000/4000, RTX 50xx GeForce). It has: - **No tensor memory (TMEM)** - **No tcgen05 instructions** - **No async warp-group MMA (wgmma)** Memory routes are Hopper-style (TMA + cp.async); compute is Ampere-style (warp shuffle + warp MMA `mma.sync.aligned.kind::mxf4nvf4...m16n8k64`).

payload.observed: - Compiler errors looking for `tcgen05_mma`, `make_tmem_load_atom`, descriptor-based MMA operands that don't exist on sm_120 - For NVFP4 / blockscaled paths, generated PTX uses TMEM accumulators that crash on launch
